subject: AWS private offer: add-on SKUs, partner margin smoothing, escrow pricing
messages:
From: Ashton Cole <ashton@magnacloud.com>

Cc: Jill Harper <jill.harper@enterprise-tech.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 15:22:00 -0400
Subject: Private offer questions — add-on SKUs, partner margin smoothing, escrow pricing

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team liked the latency numbers. We're working internally on packaging for our fleet rollout and have a few specific asks before we can move to PO. Can you confirm the following for an AWS private offer?

1) Add-on SKUs: We expect to buy a core committed tier (reserved capacity) and then buy several add-on SKUs (embedding ops, real-time chat slots). Do you support pricing the add-ons as a % of the core SKU list price (e.g., add-on = core * 0.25) instead of absolute per-unit prices? If so, does that map straight into the private offer JSON or do we need separate SKUs?

2) Partner margin smoothing: our reseller wants a predictable margin over the first 6 months while usage ramps. Is there a recommended passback schedule (e.g., 70% of partner commission in month 1 gradually ramp to 100% month 6) Redwood supports in the PO mechanics?

3) Escrow/list price anchoring: procurement asked whether Redwood can set a list price floor in the PO and hold a small escrow credit to be used for overage true-ups. Any template language or impacts to revenue recognition we should be aware of?

We've sketched expected volumes and a target commit in the attached workbook. Can you take a first pass and let us know what structure you'd recommend?

Thanks —
Ashton
Director of Cloud Procurement
MagnaCloud
[Attachment: magna_usage_estimates.csv (csv)]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer questions — add-on SKUs, partner margin smoothing, escrow pricing

Hi Ashton —

Appreciate the details and the workbook. Short answer: yes, we can support each of these approaches, but there are trade-offs. Below is a pragmatic structure we typically recommend for AWS private offers when customers want predictable partner economics and simple ops for add-ons.

Proposed approach (high-level):
- Commit tier (core SKU): list price per unit, standard reserved terms. This is the PO anchor.
- Add-on SKUs: we recommend modeling add-ons as distinct SKUs in the PO but generated with list prices derived from the core SKU (we can automate this in the offer template). That keeps accounting clean while allowing you to express add-ons as a % in the negotiation.
- Partner margin smoothing: two options we support
  * Time-based passback (recommended): set a partner passback schedule in the private offer ops fields — e.g., 70% of the committed commission paid in month 1, then linear ramp to 100% by month 6. Redwood will output monthly commission lines so your reseller can predict cash flow.
  * Credit escrow with true-up: Redwood can accept a small holdback that is released on a successful ramp/true-up. This is heavier to implement but reduces month-to-month reconciliation work.
- Escrow/list price anchoring: we recommend a small non-refundable list-price floor (a minimal list price delta) and an escrow credit on the PO for overage protection. This keeps your list prices stable for marketplace SKUs while providing a runway for true-up. Finance/legal should review the template; I’ve looped Laura.

Next steps: I attached a worked example where I converted your workbook numbers into a draft private-offer template and a channel-margin model. If this approach looks right I can spin up a draft PO (AWS private-offer JSON) and a DocuSign term sheet.

Cheers,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales — Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pricing_workbook_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Subject: Re: Private offer questions — margin math and suggested passback cadence

FWIW I took a run at the math in the attached CSV. Key points:

- If add-ons are priced at core * 0.25, partner effective margin (gross) is ~18–22% depending on the mix.
- For smoothing, recommended passback cadence for a first-year ramp: 70%/80%/90%/95%/100%/100% across months 1–6. That hits partner cash sooner while protecting Redwood against initial shortfalls.
- List-price floor suggestion: keep add-on list price >= 20% of core list to avoid sub-revenue scenarios once commissions are applied.

I'll attach the margin model so you can tweak assumptions. Happy to hop on a 30-min call and walk through the sensitivity.

Best,
Ben Carter
Channel Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: channel_margin_model.csv (spreadsheet)]

Subject: Re: Private offer questions — legal/finance flags on escrow and recognition

Hi Ashton and team —

Thanks for the thoughtful approach — happy to see the passback options. A couple finance/legal flags to note before we send a DocuSign: 

1) Escrow treatment: if Redwood is holding an escrow credit on the PO, we need clear release criteria and accounting treatment. Our preference is a small pre-funded credit (applied to the invoice) rather than a separate custodial escrow, as that avoids an additional liability account. If you require a true escrow we’ll need departmental sign-off and a statement of how it moves from deferred revenue/escrow into recognized revenue.

2) List-price anchoring and marketplace compliance: AWS requires marketplace list price to be defensible. If you plan to keep a floor, procurement needs to confirm the commercial rationale. We can bake a limited-term list-price override into the private-offer metadata, but it must be time-boxed (e.g., 12 months) and have a true-up path.

3) DocuSign & PO flow: to keep this clean from an audit perspective we recommend Redwood generate the private-offer JSON and an accompanying term sheet PDF. Attach the PDF to DocuSign; the PO JSON should be stored in the deal record for ops.

I've attached a sample term sheet that we can adapt. If you want, Vivek and I can join a 30-min call tomorrow to lock language.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

- Can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to accept a pre-funded credit on the initial invoice (we prefer this to a third-party escrow) and include the release schedule in the term sheet?

If you can get the draft PO + DocuSign by end of day tomorrow we’ll route to our legal and marketplace teams and aim to sign next week.

Appreciate it —
Ashton
